mechanism_narrative: The sharp recent decline in WORKPLACES from t-3w to t-0w will keep weekday foot traffic weak, but the slower fall in RETAIL_REC than WORKPLACES implies retail demand is stabilizing and should edge higher over the next four weeks as commuting losses stop worsening.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES continues falling or does not stabilize, the trend-signal hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays above +10 while WORKPLACES stays below -30, discretionary trips are substituted toward at-home activity and local necessities, which suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +10 and WORKPLACES stays below -30
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises for two consecutive weekly means while RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 and WORKPLACES remains below -30, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT below -50 points from baseline signals tighter movement restraint and fewer cross-town shopping trips, which should pull RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -50 yet RETAIL_REC is higher than in the prior four-week window, the restraint channel is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rebounds while GROCERY_PHARM remains near its current mild decline, households are reallocating outings toward outdoor leisure rather than shopping, which should reduce RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by 5 points or more and RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next one to two weeks, the leisure-substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in GROCERY_PHARM indicates more routine neighborhood errand traffic and often precedes broader local spending, so RETAIL_REC should increase over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior four-week mean over the next month, the spillover claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weaken together, the combined reduction in commute-linked exposure lowers incidental retail visits, so RETAIL_REC will continue falling over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline but RETAIL_REC rises within the next two weekly means, the commute-exposure mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under reopening, a sustained rise in WORKPLACES from the current depressed level should increase weekday shopping and lunch trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 5 points from its current weekly mean
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises by 5 points or more during reopening but RETAIL_REC remains below its last-four-week mean after four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The recent pattern of smaller declines in RETAIL_REC alongside improving RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests local substitution is already saturated; if RESIDENTIAL stops rising and TRANSIT remains depressed, RETAIL_REC will stay flat to slightly lower over the next one week.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL holds flat or falls while TRANSIT remains depressed but RETAIL_REC rises in the next weekly mean, the saturation claim is rejected.
